tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# KINTSUGI‑Ω Execution & Build Plan

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **Approved by the Architect** (Surya Prasanth R, @suryaprasanthcse), 2026‑10‑11 |
| Specification | `../Blueprint_Omega_Master.md` (v1.0, full version). This plan reconciles it with the verified environment; it does not dilute it. |
| Visual archive | `../kintsugi-omega-blueprints/kintsugi-omega-blueprint-img_{1..12}.png` |
| Scope | Full Blueprint Omega. No reduced cut. |

This file is the in-tree source of truth for every interactive or headless session. Amendments discovered during execution are appended to the **Amendments log** at the end, never edited into the approved text.

---

## 0. Schedule constraint

- Plan approval: 12:27 IST, Oct 11. Submission window closes 23:55 IST, Oct 12 (about 35½ h).
- The specification itself estimates about 4 engineer-weeks for the full build (§13.2 R1, "Certain"). The estimate for Stages 1–13 below is 45–50 h of continuous wall-clock work.
- The autonomy window W must end by about 19:55 IST Oct 12 to leave about 4 h for reveals, audit, video and submission. Therefore **T0 ≤ 19:55 IST Oct 12 − W**.
- W and T0 are decided at the Stage 8 go/no-go gate (ruling D1).

## 1. Verified environment baseline (pre-Stage 1)

| Area | Verified state |
|---|---|
| Entire | CLI 0.11.4 and entire-graph v0.4.0 (`no_egress: true`). Checkpoints are per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-2-chars>/<ULID>`, not the legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. No `rewind` command exists. Available: `entire checkpoint explain --json/--transcript`, `entire why <file>:<line> --json`, `entire session resume/stop`. |
| Entire behaviour | A mid-turn commit is linked only when the files were edited with Claude Code's Edit/Write tools. Each Stop hook adds a "Finalize transcript" commit, which moves the checkpoint ref. The pre-push hook only pushes refs in its local queue. Built-in redaction blanks secret-looking lines even with zero configured rules. |
| Windows | Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` blocks on a hidden `CONIN$` prompt unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`. The Claude desktop app is MSIX-packaged and virtualizes `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` writes, so tooling lives under `~/.local/share` (`UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`). |
| Tools present | `claude` 2.1.269 (headless CLI; the desktop app runs 2.1.295), Node, npm, git 2.55. Docker Desktop installed, engine stopped. WSL2 distros Ubuntu and docker-desktop (stopped). |
| Tools missing | `temporal`, `gh`, `make` (Windows), `age` CLI (the `pyrage` library replaces it). |
| Python | uv-managed CPython 3.12.14, pinned by `.python-version`. |
| Commit policy | Sole author and committer: Surya Prasanth R `<suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>`. Never `Co-authored-by:`. Attribution only through `Entire-Checkpoint:` and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |

## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation

### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3

- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

## 3. Architect rulings D1–D8

| # | Decision | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | W length and T0 | Deferred to the Stage 8 go/no-go gate, once the C1–C14 mutation checks are green. |
| D2 | Runtime platform | Stages 1–2 stay cross-platform through `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py` so local Windows execution works. Prepare WSL2 Ubuntu + Docker/gVisor for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run. |
| D3 | Repo layout | Build the hosts (`hosts/ledger`, `hosts/scout`, `hosts/triage`), the antibody library (`antibodies/`) and the sabotage log (`sabotage-log/`) inside the `kintsugi-omega` monorepo first, so `suryaprasanthcse/kintsugi-omega` is self-contained and runnable from a single clone. Remote repo adapters are configurable once the GitHub token is provided. |
| D4 | Commit identity | `Surya Prasanth R <suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>` is the sole git author and committer on all commits. Never a bot contributor, never `Co-authored-by:`. Machine origin is proven by Ed25519 signatures (`.kintsugi/attest.pub`), `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |
| D5 | Ledger location | An unprotected, append-only `ledger` branch for ledger entries and anchors. |
| D6 | Temporal deployment | Implement both the deterministic `sqlite_fsm.py` WAL state machine and the Temporal workflow/activity definitions, using the single-binary Temporal CLI dev server or Docker Compose when started in Stage 5. |
| D7 | Headless Claude billing | The existing Claude Code login for Stage 2 headless spikes; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with a hard daily dollar cap in `kintsugi/sandbox/llm_proxy.py` and `kintsugi/econ/governor.py` from Stage 3/6. |
| D8 | Parallel build lanes | Approved where safe, provided every commit is made cleanly with `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, carries a verified `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and credits lines accurately. |

## 4. Stages

"Rehearsal" means an unsealed, clearly labelled practice run before T0.

### Stage 1 — Foundation and deterministic cores (no credentials)

- **Builds:** `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, ruff, pyright, `Makefile` (judge, audit, demo, fleet-up/down, check), `.github/workflows/omega-ci.yml`, `kintsugi/cli.py`, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, `kintsugi/proof/{canonical,ledger,sealed,attest,bundle}.py`, `kintsugi/stats/{mcnemar,sprt,power,holm,wilson,bootstrap}.py`, `kintsugi/econ/{governor,wright}.py`, `kintsugi/memory/{antibody,motif}.py`, `kintsugi/control/states.py`, `schemas/E1–E6`, `.kintsugi/protected_paths.yaml`.

- **Verified by:** SPRT boundaries 2.890/−2.251, steps +0.6931/−0.0660, accept after 35 clean runs, reject at n=8 (LLR 3.268), accept at n=46 (LLR −2.275); Connor n=34; McNemar b=26, c=1 → p≈2.09e-7; governor reproduces §6.2 (Pool $71.70, Cap/B $12.40) and §6.8 (B $4.83, T1 $2.34, GM 78.6%); Wright fit recovers b; RFC 8785 vectors; ledger tamper detected at the exact seq; commit-reveal and Ed25519 round-trip; property test: every state path terminates. Spike N3 is checked on the first commit.

WSL2 + Docker + gVisor integration (D2). Remote repo adapters stay configurable (D3).

definition.description:
Execute Python code in sandboxed environment with AWS API access via `call_boto3`. No network except `call_boto3`.

```python
async def call_boto3(
    *,
    service_name: str,
    operation_name: str,
    region_name: str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
) -> dict: ...
```

``operation_name`` MUST be the PascalCase AWS API operation name (e.g. ``ListBuckets``,
``GetTable``, ``StartQueryExecution``). Do not use the snake_case boto3 method name
(``list_buckets``, ``get_table``); exact matches are corrected only as a runtime fallback.

Response includes `api_calls` list—verify APIs ran before trusting `return_value`.

REQUIRED PATTERNS:
- Return `result={...}` then `result` alone as final expression
- Call each API once; results auto-paginate
- Return ALL resources—missing one is wrong
- Return raw data fields; let LLM judge thresholds
- Use `asyncio.gather(*[...])` with `return_exceptions=True` for reads; let mutations raise

⚠️ LIST→DESCRIBE: List* returns only names/ARNs. Use Get*/Describe* for attributes.

⚠️ CONTENTS vs CONTAINER: "empty buckets"→ListObjects; "records"→Scan; "X configured"→Get*Configuration.

RULES:
1. SELF-CONTAINED: Discover resources inside script.
2. ALL-REGIONS: DescribeRegions→gather per region.
3. PERMISSIONS: All policies ONE script. `bucket`≠`bucket/*`. Report YES/PARTIAL/NO.

PRE-IMPORTED: asyncio, collections, csv, dataclasses, datetime, decimal, enum, fractions, functools, itertools, json, math, re, statistics, string, time, typing, uuid, ClientError, io.StringIO, io.BytesIO.

BUILTIN MODULES: AWS teams provide higher-level functions for complex jobs. Find out more with:

```python
import aws_mcp
help(aws_mcp)
```

To search for available functions:

```python
await aws_mcp.search_functions("search query in natural language")
```

content.content:
"""The cfo.ai model (Stage 9, spec §4.6.4): unit economics, runway, scenarios, plan vs actual.

cfo.ai's Ari MCP (spike A8) is not wired in this edition, so the sync is a file export the
Architect imports: ``business/cfo_export/`` holds one CSV per tab, each derived from
``business/plan.json`` and the actuals and nothing else:

- ``unit_economics.csv``: per host, price, C_mon, the observed primary and secondary response
  costs (c_p, c_s) with their sample sizes and phase, E[C] = q·c_s + (1 − q)·c_p at the
  observed coverage, the month's incident cost, COGS and gross margin against the floor.
- ``scenarios.csv``: the same at coverage q ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9} (spec §3.5.5).
- ``runway.csv``: months of runway from the plan's cash and fixed costs; while either is null
  the row says so instead of inventing a number.
- ``plan_vs_actual.csv``: per host and month, the planned C_mon and repair pool against the
  actual operating cost and repair-side spend.
- ``wright.json`` beside them: the nightly learning-curve refit.

``write_export`` is what ``kintsugi econ cfo-export`` runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from kintsugi.econ import governor, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

SCENARIO_Q = (0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
EXPORT_DIR = Path("business") / "cfo_export"


def _csv(header: Sequence[str], rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]]) -> str:
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(header)
    writer.writerows(rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def _money(x: float) -> str:
    return f"{x:.4f}"


def observed_coverage(actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> float:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    total = int(units["primary_n"]) + int(units["secondary_n"])
    return int(units["secondary_n"]) / total if total else 0.0


def economics_row(plan: BusinessPlan, host: str, c_p: float, c_s: float, q: float,
                  ) -> dict[str, float]:  # fmt: skip
    h = plan.host(host)
    e_cost = governor.expected_incident_cost(q, c_s, c_p)
    incidents = h.expected_remaining_incidents
    cogs = h.c_mon_usd_month + e_cost * incidents
    return {"e_cost": e_cost, "incident_month": e_cost * incidents, "cogs": cogs,
            "gm": governor.gross_margin(h.price_usd_month, cogs)}  # fmt: skip


def unit_economics(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        h = plan.host(host)
        row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
        meets = "yes" if row["gm"] >= plan.gm_floor else "no"
        rows.append([host, h.tier, _money(h.price_usd_month), _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                     _money(c_p), units["primary_n"], _money(c_s), units["secondary_n"],
                     phase or "all", f"{q:.3f}", _money(row["e_cost"]),
                     f"{h.expected_remaining_incidents:g}", _money(row["incident_month"]),
                     _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}",
                     f"{100 * plan.gm_floor:.1f}", meets])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "tier", "price_usd_month", "c_mon_usd_month", "c_primary_usd",
              "primary_n", "c_secondary_usd", "secondary_n", "cost_phase", "coverage_q",
              "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incidents_month", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct", "gm_floor_pct", "meets_floor")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def scenarios(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        for q in SCENARIO_Q:
            row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
            rows.append([host, f"{q:.1f}", _money(row["e_cost"]), _money(row["incident_month"]),
                         _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}"])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "coverage_q", "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def runway(plan_data: Mapping[str, Any], plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals,
           phase: str | None) -> str:  # fmt: skip
    company = plan_data.get("company") or {}
    cash, fixed = company.get("cash_usd"), company.get("fixed_costs_usd_month")
    header = ("cash_usd", "fixed_costs_usd_month", "revenue_usd_month", "cogs_usd_month",
              "net_burn_usd_month", "runway_months", "status")  # fmt: skip
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    revenue = sum(plan.host(h).price_usd_month for h in plan.hosts)
    cogs = sum(economics_row(plan, h, c_p, c_s, q)["cogs"] for h in plan.hosts)
    if cash is None or fixed is None:
        return _csv(header, [["", "", _money(revenue), _money(cogs), "", "",
                              "set company.cash_usd and company.fixed_costs_usd_month in "
                              "business/plan.json"]])  # fmt: skip
    burn = float(fixed) + cogs - revenue
    months = "infinite" if burn <= 0 else f"{float(cash) / burn:.1f}"
    return _csv(header, [[_money(float(cash)), _money(float(fixed)), _money(revenue),
                          _money(cogs), _money(burn), months, "computed"]])  # fmt: skip


def plan_vs_actual(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals) -> str:
    months = sorted({s.month for s in actuals.spends})
    rows = []
    for month in months:
        for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
            h = plan.host(host)
            planned_pool = governor.pool(h.price_usd_month, plan.gm_floor, h.c_mon_usd_month)
            rehearsal = actuals.total(host=host, month=month, phase="rehearsal")
            spent = actuals.month_to_date(host, month)
            rows.append([month, host, _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                         _money(actuals.operating_cost(host, month)), _money(planned_pool),
                         _money(spent), _money(rehearsal)])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("month", "host", "planned_c_mon_usd", "actual_operating_usd",
              "planned_repair_pool_usd", "actual_repair_spend_usd",
              "rehearsal_spend_usd")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def learning_curve(actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every response's cost in the order it happened (date, then source run)."""
    lines = sorted(actuals.select(phase=None, kinds=("repair", "vaccination")),
                   key=lambda s: (s.date, s.source, s.ref))  # fmt: skip
    found = wright.refit([s.usd for s in lines])
    found["refs"] = [s.ref for s in lines]
    found["phases"] = sorted({s.phase for s in lines})
    return found


def export(plan_path: Path, actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The export's files and their contents (paths relative to ``business/cfo_export``)."""
    data = json.loads(Path(plan_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    live = bool(actuals.select(kinds=("repair", "vaccination")))
    phase = "live" if live else None  # until W runs, the rehearsals are the only observations
    meta = {"business_plan_sha": plan.sha, "cost_phase": phase or "all (rehearsal only)",
            "observed_coverage_q": round(observed_coverage(actuals, phase), 6),
            "unit_costs": actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)}  # fmt: skip
    return {
        "unit_economics.csv": unit_economics(plan, actuals, phase),
        "scenarios.csv": scenarios(plan, actuals, phase),
        "runway.csv": runway(data, plan, actuals, phase),
        "plan_vs_actual.csv": plan_vs_actual(plan, actuals),
        "wright.json": json.dumps(learning_curve(actuals), indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        "meta.json": json.dumps(meta, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    }


def write_export(repo: Path, actuals: Actuals, out: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    folder = out or Path(repo) / EXPORT_DIR
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []
    for name, text in export(Path(repo) / "business" / "plan.json", actuals).items():
        (folder / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(folder / name)
    return written
"""The cfo.ai export and the nightly Wright refit (Stage 9)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from kintsugi.cli import main
from kintsugi.econ import cfo_sync, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals, Spend
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PLAN = REPO / "business" / "plan.json"
EXPORT = REPO / "business" / "cfo_export"


def _rows(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)))


def test_the_committed_export_is_what_the_plan_and_actuals_give() -> None:
    files = cfo_sync.export(PLAN, Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json"))
    assert sorted(files) == sorted(p.name for p in EXPORT.iterdir())
    for name, text in files.items():
        assert (EXPORT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == text, name
    meta = json.loads(files["meta.json"])
    assert meta["business_plan_sha"] == BusinessPlan.load(PLAN).sha
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "all (rehearsal only)"  # no live spend before W
    triage = next(r for r in _rows(files["unit_economics.csv"]) if r["host"] == "triage")
    assert triage["meets_floor"] == "yes"
    assert float(triage["gross_margin_pct"]) >= 70.0
    assert len(_rows(files["scenarios.csv"])) == 3 * len(cfo_sync.SCENARIO_Q)
    assert "set company.cash_usd" in _rows(files["runway.csv"])[0]["status"]


def test_runway_is_computed_only_from_the_architects_numbers() -> None:
    data = json.loads(PLAN.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data["company"] = {"cash_usd": 10000.0, "fixed_costs_usd_month": 1000.0}
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    actuals = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json")
    row = _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]
    burn = 1000.0 + float(row["cogs_usd_month"]) - 697.0
    assert row["status"] == "computed"
    assert float(row["runway_months"]) == pytest.approx(10000.0 / burn, abs=0.05)
    data["company"]["fixed_costs_usd_month"] = 0.0
    assert _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]["runway_months"] == "infinite"


def test_live_spend_replaces_the_rehearsal_unit_costs() -> None:
    live = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json").add(
        Spend("2026-10-20", "triage", "repair", 2.0, "INC-0001", "case"),
        Spend("2026-10-21", "scout", "vaccination", 0.2, "VAC-AB-2-scout", "case"),
    )
    meta = json.loads(cfo_sync.export(PLAN, live)["meta.json"])
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "live"
    assert meta["unit_costs"]["primary_mean_usd"] == 2.0
    assert meta["observed_coverage_q"] == 0.5


def test_the_refit_needs_three_points_and_recovers_the_exponent() -> None:
    assert wright.refit([1.0, 0.5])["status"] == "insufficient"
    costs = [wright.predict(n, 10.0, 0.4) for n in range(1, 9)]
    found = wright.refit(costs)
    assert found["status"] == "fitted"
    assert found["b"] == pytest.approx(0.4, abs=1e-6)
    assert found["progress_ratio"] == pytest.approx(2**-0.4, abs=1e-6)


def test_the_econ_commands(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path,
                           capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:  # fmt: skip
    monkeypatch.chdir(REPO)
    assert main(["econ", "refit"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["n_points"] == 4
    assert main(["econ", "cfo-export", "--out", str(tmp_path / "cfo")]) == 0
    assert (tmp_path / "cfo" / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        EXPORT / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # fmt: skip
    capsys.readouterr()
    assert main(["econ", "actuals"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["rehearsal"]["secondary_n"] == 2

"""The cfo.ai model (Stage 9, spec §4.6.4): unit economics, runway, scenarios, plan vs actual.

cfo.ai's Ari MCP (spike A8) is not wired in this edition, so the sync is a file export the
Architect imports: ``business/cfo_export/`` holds one CSV per tab, each derived from
``business/plan.json`` and the actuals and nothing else:

- ``unit_economics.csv``: per host, price, C_mon, the observed primary and secondary response
  costs (c_p, c_s) with their sample sizes and phase, E[C] = q·c_s + (1 − q)·c_p at the
  observed coverage, the month's incident cost, COGS and gross margin against the floor.
- ``scenarios.csv``: the same at coverage q ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9} (spec §3.5.5).
- ``runway.csv``: months of runway from the plan's cash and fixed costs; while either is null
  the row says so instead of inventing a number.
- ``plan_vs_actual.csv``: per host and month, the planned C_mon and repair pool against the
  actual operating cost and repair-side spend.
- ``wright.json`` beside them: the nightly learning-curve refit.

``write_export`` is what ``kintsugi econ cfo-export`` runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from kintsugi.econ import governor, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

SCENARIO_Q = (0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
EXPORT_DIR = Path("business") / "cfo_export"


def _csv(header: Sequence[str], rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]]) -> str:
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(header)
    writer.writerows(rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def _money(x: float) -> str:
    return f"{x:.4f}"


def observed_coverage(actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> float:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    total = int(units["primary_n"]) + int(units["secondary_n"])
    return int(units["secondary_n"]) / total if total else 0.0


def economics_row(plan: BusinessPlan, host: str, c_p: float, c_s: float, q: float,
                  ) -> dict[str, float]:  # fmt: skip
    h = plan.host(host)
    e_cost = governor.expected_incident_cost(q, c_s, c_p)
    incidents = h.expected_remaining_incidents
    cogs = h.c_mon_usd_month + e_cost * incidents
    return {"e_cost": e_cost, "incident_month": e_cost * incidents, "cogs": cogs,
            "gm": governor.gross_margin(h.price_usd_month, cogs)}  # fmt: skip


def unit_economics(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        h = plan.host(host)
        row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
        meets = "yes" if row["gm"] >= plan.gm_floor else "no"
        rows.append([host, h.tier, _money(h.price_usd_month), _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                     _money(c_p), units["primary_n"], _money(c_s), units["secondary_n"],
                     phase or "all", f"{q:.3f}", _money(row["e_cost"]),
                     f"{h.expected_remaining_incidents:g}", _money(row["incident_month"]),
                     _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}",
                     f"{100 * plan.gm_floor:.1f}", meets])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "tier", "price_usd_month", "c_mon_usd_month", "c_primary_usd",
              "primary_n", "c_secondary_usd", "secondary_n", "cost_phase", "coverage_q",
              "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incidents_month", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct", "gm_floor_pct", "meets_floor")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def scenarios(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        for q in SCENARIO_Q:
            row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
            rows.append([host, f"{q:.1f}", _money(row["e_cost"]), _money(row["incident_month"]),
                         _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}"])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "coverage_q", "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def runway(plan_data: Mapping[str, Any], plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals,
           phase: str | None) -> str:  # fmt: skip
    company = plan_data.get("company") or {}
    cash, fixed = company.get("cash_usd"), company.get("fixed_costs_usd_month")
    header = ("cash_usd", "fixed_costs_usd_month", "revenue_usd_month", "cogs_usd_month",
              "net_burn_usd_month", "runway_months", "status")  # fmt: skip
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    revenue = sum(plan.host(h).price_usd_month for h in plan.hosts)
    cogs = sum(economics_row(plan, h, c_p, c_s, q)["cogs"] for h in plan.hosts)
    if cash is None or fixed is None:
        return _csv(header, [["", "", _money(revenue), _money(cogs), "", "",
                              "set company.cash_usd and company.fixed_costs_usd_month in "
                              "business/plan.json"]])  # fmt: skip
    burn = float(fixed) + cogs - revenue
    months = "infinite" if burn <= 0 else f"{float(cash) / burn:.1f}"
    return _csv(header, [[_money(float(cash)), _money(float(fixed)), _money(revenue),
                          _money(cogs), _money(burn), months, "computed"]])  # fmt: skip


def plan_vs_actual(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals) -> str:
    months = sorted({s.month for s in actuals.spends})
    rows = []
    for month in months:
        for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
            h = plan.host(host)
            planned_pool = governor.pool(h.price_usd_month, plan.gm_floor, h.c_mon_usd_month)
            rehearsal = actuals.total(host=host, month=month, phase="rehearsal")
            spent = actuals.month_to_date(host, month)
            rows.append([month, host, _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                         _money(actuals.operating_cost(host, month)), _money(planned_pool),
                         _money(spent), _money(rehearsal)])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("month", "host", "planned_c_mon_usd", "actual_operating_usd",
              "planned_repair_pool_usd", "actual_repair_spend_usd",
              "rehearsal_spend_usd")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def learning_curve(actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every response's cost in the order it happened (date, then source run)."""
    lines = sorted(actuals.select(phase=None, kinds=("repair", "vaccination")),
                   key=lambda s: (s.date, s.source, s.ref))  # fmt: skip
    found = wright.refit([s.usd for s in lines])
    found["refs"] = [s.ref for s in lines]
    found["phases"] = sorted({s.phase for s in lines})
    return found


def export(plan_path: Path, actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The export's files and their contents (paths relative to ``business/cfo_export``)."""
    data = json.loads(Path(plan_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    live = bool(actuals.select(kinds=("repair", "vaccination")))
    phase = "live" if live else None  # until W runs, the rehearsals are the only observations
    meta = {"business_plan_sha": plan.sha, "cost_phase": phase or "all (rehearsal only)",
            "observed_coverage_q": round(observed_coverage(actuals, phase), 6),
            "unit_costs": actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)}  # fmt: skip
    return {
        "unit_economics.csv": unit_economics(plan, actuals, phase),
        "scenarios.csv": scenarios(plan, actuals, phase),
        "runway.csv": runway(data, plan, actuals, phase),
        "plan_vs_actual.csv": plan_vs_actual(plan, actuals),
        "wright.json": json.dumps(learning_curve(actuals), indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        "meta.json": json.dumps(meta, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    }


def write_export(repo: Path, actuals: Actuals, out: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    folder = out or Path(repo) / EXPORT_DIR
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []
    for name, text in export(Path(repo) / "business" / "plan.json", actuals).items():
        (folder / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(folder / name)
    return written
"""The cfo.ai export and the nightly Wright refit (Stage 9)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from kintsugi.cli import main
from kintsugi.econ import cfo_sync, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals, Spend
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PLAN = REPO / "business" / "plan.json"
EXPORT = REPO / "business" / "cfo_export"


def _rows(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)))


def test_the_committed_export_is_what_the_plan_and_actuals_give() -> None:
    files = cfo_sync.export(PLAN, Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json"))
    assert sorted(files) == sorted(p.name for p in EXPORT.iterdir())
    for name, text in files.items():
        assert (EXPORT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == text, name
    meta = json.loads(files["meta.json"])
    assert meta["business_plan_sha"] == BusinessPlan.load(PLAN).sha
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "all (rehearsal only)"  # no live spend before W
    triage = next(r for r in _rows(files["unit_economics.csv"]) if r["host"] == "triage")
    assert triage["meets_floor"] == "yes"
    assert float(triage["gross_margin_pct"]) >= 70.0
    assert len(_rows(files["scenarios.csv"])) == 3 * len(cfo_sync.SCENARIO_Q)
    assert "set company.cash_usd" in _rows(files["runway.csv"])[0]["status"]


def test_runway_is_computed_only_from_the_architects_numbers() -> None:
    data = json.loads(PLAN.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data["company"] = {"cash_usd": 10000.0, "fixed_costs_usd_month": 1000.0}
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    actuals = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json")
    row = _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]
    burn = 1000.0 + float(row["cogs_usd_month"]) - 697.0
    assert row["status"] == "computed"
    assert float(row["runway_months"]) == pytest.approx(10000.0 / burn, abs=0.05)
    data["company"]["fixed_costs_usd_month"] = 0.0
    assert _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]["runway_months"] == "infinite"


def test_live_spend_replaces_the_rehearsal_unit_costs() -> None:
    live = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json").add(
        Spend("2026-10-20", "triage", "repair", 2.0, "INC-0001", "case"),
        Spend("2026-10-21", "scout", "vaccination", 0.2, "VAC-AB-2-scout", "case"),
    )
    meta = json.loads(cfo_sync.export(PLAN, live)["meta.json"])
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "live"
    assert meta["unit_costs"]["primary_mean_usd"] == 2.0
    assert meta["observed_coverage_q"] == 0.5


def test_the_refit_needs_three_points_and_recovers_the_exponent() -> None:
    assert wright.refit([1.0, 0.5])["status"] == "insufficient"
    costs = [wright.predict(n, 10.0, 0.4) for n in range(1, 9)]
    found = wright.refit(costs)
    assert found["status"] == "fitted"
    assert found["b"] == pytest.approx(0.4, abs=1e-6)
    assert found["progress_ratio"] == pytest.approx(2**-0.4, abs=1e-6)


def test_the_econ_commands(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path,
                           capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:  # fmt: skip
    monkeypatch.chdir(REPO)
    assert main(["econ", "refit"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["n_points"] == 4
    assert main(["econ", "cfo-export", "--out", str(tmp_path / "cfo")]) == 0
    assert (tmp_path / "cfo" / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        EXPORT / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # fmt: skip
    capsys.readouterr()
    assert main(["econ", "actuals"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["rehearsal"]["secondary_n"] == 2

"""The cfo.ai model (Stage 9, spec §4.6.4): unit economics, runway, scenarios, plan vs actual.

cfo.ai's Ari MCP (spike A8) is not wired in this edition, so the sync is a file export the
Architect imports: ``business/cfo_export/`` holds one CSV per tab, each derived from
``business/plan.json`` and the actuals and nothing else:

- ``unit_economics.csv``: per host, price, C_mon, the observed primary and secondary response
  costs (c_p, c_s) with their sample sizes and phase, E[C] = q·c_s + (1 − q)·c_p at the
  observed coverage, the month's incident cost, COGS and gross margin against the floor.
- ``scenarios.csv``: the same at coverage q ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9} (spec §3.5.5).
- ``runway.csv``: months of runway from the plan's cash and fixed costs; while either is null
  the row says so instead of inventing a number.
- ``plan_vs_actual.csv``: per host and month, the planned C_mon and repair pool against the
  actual operating cost and repair-side spend.
- ``wright.json`` beside them: the nightly learning-curve refit.

``write_export`` is what ``kintsugi econ cfo-export`` runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from kintsugi.econ import governor, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

SCENARIO_Q = (0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
EXPORT_DIR = Path("business") / "cfo_export"


def _csv(header: Sequence[str], rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]]) -> str:
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(header)
    writer.writerows(rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def _money(x: float) -> str:
    return f"{x:.4f}"


def observed_coverage(actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> float:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    total = int(units["primary_n"]) + int(units["secondary_n"])
    return int(units["secondary_n"]) / total if total else 0.0


def economics_row(plan: BusinessPlan, host: str, c_p: float, c_s: float, q: float,
                  ) -> dict[str, float]:  # fmt: skip
    h = plan.host(host)
    e_cost = governor.expected_incident_cost(q, c_s, c_p)
    incidents = h.expected_remaining_incidents
    cogs = h.c_mon_usd_month + e_cost * incidents
    return {"e_cost": e_cost, "incident_month": e_cost * incidents, "cogs": cogs,
            "gm": governor.gross_margin(h.price_usd_month, cogs)}  # fmt: skip


def unit_economics(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        h = plan.host(host)
        row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
        meets = "yes" if row["gm"] >= plan.gm_floor else "no"
        rows.append([host, h.tier, _money(h.price_usd_month), _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                     _money(c_p), units["primary_n"], _money(c_s), units["secondary_n"],
                     phase or "all", f"{q:.3f}", _money(row["e_cost"]),
                     f"{h.expected_remaining_incidents:g}", _money(row["incident_month"]),
                     _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}",
                     f"{100 * plan.gm_floor:.1f}", meets])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "tier", "price_usd_month", "c_mon_usd_month", "c_primary_usd",
              "primary_n", "c_secondary_usd", "secondary_n", "cost_phase", "coverage_q",
              "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incidents_month", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct", "gm_floor_pct", "meets_floor")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def scenarios(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        for q in SCENARIO_Q:
            row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
            rows.append([host, f"{q:.1f}", _money(row["e_cost"]), _money(row["incident_month"]),
                         _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}"])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "coverage_q", "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def runway(plan_data: Mapping[str, Any], plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals,
           phase: str | None) -> str:  # fmt: skip
    company = plan_data.get("company") or {}
    cash, fixed = company.get("cash_usd"), company.get("fixed_costs_usd_month")
    header = ("cash_usd", "fixed_costs_usd_month", "revenue_usd_month", "cogs_usd_month",
              "net_burn_usd_month", "runway_months", "status")  # fmt: skip
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    revenue = sum(plan.host(h).price_usd_month for h in plan.hosts)
    cogs = sum(economics_row(plan, h, c_p, c_s, q)["cogs"] for h in plan.hosts)
    if cash is None or fixed is None:
        return _csv(header, [["", "", _money(revenue), _money(cogs), "", "",
                              "set company.cash_usd and company.fixed_costs_usd_month in "
                              "business/plan.json"]])  # fmt: skip
    burn = float(fixed) + cogs - revenue
    months = "infinite" if burn <= 0 else f"{float(cash) / burn:.1f}"
    return _csv(header, [[_money(float(cash)), _money(float(fixed)), _money(revenue),
                          _money(cogs), _money(burn), months, "computed"]])  # fmt: skip


def plan_vs_actual(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals) -> str:
    months = sorted({s.month for s in actuals.spends})
    rows = []
    for month in months:
        for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
            h = plan.host(host)
            planned_pool = governor.pool(h.price_usd_month, plan.gm_floor, h.c_mon_usd_month)
            rehearsal = actuals.total(host=host, month=month, phase="rehearsal")
            spent = actuals.month_to_date(host, month)
            rows.append([month, host, _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                         _money(actuals.operating_cost(host, month)), _money(planned_pool),
                         _money(spent), _money(rehearsal)])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("month", "host", "planned_c_mon_usd", "actual_operating_usd",
              "planned_repair_pool_usd", "actual_repair_spend_usd",
              "rehearsal_spend_usd")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def learning_curve(actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every response's cost in the order it happened (date, then source run)."""
    lines = sorted(actuals.select(phase=None, kinds=("repair", "vaccination")),
                   key=lambda s: (s.date, s.source, s.ref))  # fmt: skip
    found = wright.refit([s.usd for s in lines])
    found["refs"] = [s.ref for s in lines]
    found["phases"] = sorted({s.phase for s in lines})
    return found


def export(plan_path: Path, actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The export's files and their contents (paths relative to ``business/cfo_export``)."""
    data = json.loads(Path(plan_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    live = bool(actuals.select(kinds=("repair", "vaccination")))
    phase = "live" if live else None  # until W runs, the rehearsals are the only observations
    meta = {"business_plan_sha": plan.sha, "cost_phase": phase or "all (rehearsal only)",
            "observed_coverage_q": round(observed_coverage(actuals, phase), 6),
            "unit_costs": actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)}  # fmt: skip
    return {
        "unit_economics.csv": unit_economics(plan, actuals, phase),
        "scenarios.csv": scenarios(plan, actuals, phase),
        "runway.csv": runway(data, plan, actuals, phase),
        "plan_vs_actual.csv": plan_vs_actual(plan, actuals),
        "wright.json": json.dumps(learning_curve(actuals), indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        "meta.json": json.dumps(meta, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    }


def write_export(repo: Path, actuals: Actuals, out: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    folder = out or Path(repo) / EXPORT_DIR
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []
    for name, text in export(Path(repo) / "business" / "plan.json", actuals).items():
        (folder / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(folder / name)
    return written

              "planned_repair_pool_usd", "actual_repair_spend_usd",
              "rehearsal_spend_usd")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def learning_curve(actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every response's cost in the order it happened (date, then source run)."""
    lines = sorted(actuals.select(phase=None, kinds=("repair", "vaccination")),
                   key=lambda s: (s.date, s.source, s.ref))  # fmt: skip
    found = wright.refit([s.usd for s in lines])
    found["refs"] = [s.ref for s in lines]
    found["phases"] = sorted({s.phase for s in lines})
    return found


def export(plan_path: Path, actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The export's files and their contents (paths relative to ``business/cfo_export``)."""

            "observed_coverage_q": round(observed_coverage(actuals, phase), 6),

    return {
        "unit_economics.csv": unit_economics(plan, actuals, phase),
        "scenarios.csv": scenarios(plan, actuals, phase),
        "runway.csv": runway(data, plan, actuals, phase),
        "plan_vs_actual.csv": plan_vs_actual(plan, actuals),
        "wright.json": json.dumps(learning_curve(actuals), indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        "meta.json": json.dumps(meta, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    }


def write_export(repo: Path, actuals: Actuals, out: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    folder = out or Path(repo) / EXPORT_DIR

        (folder / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(folder / name)
    return written

"""The cfo.ai model (Stage 9, spec §4.6.4): unit economics, runway, scenarios, plan vs actual.

cfo.ai's Ari MCP (spike A8) is not wired in this edition, so the sync is a file export the
Architect imports: ``business/cfo_export/`` holds one CSV per tab, each derived from
``business/plan.json`` and the actuals and nothing else:

- ``unit_economics.csv``: per host, price, C_mon, the observed primary and secondary response
  costs (c_p, c_s) with their sample sizes and phase, E[C] = q·c_s + (1 − q)·c_p at the
  observed coverage, the month's incident cost, COGS and gross margin against the floor.
- ``scenarios.csv``: the same at coverage q ∈ {0.3, 0.7, 0.9} (spec §3.5.5).
- ``runway.csv``: months of runway from the plan's cash and fixed costs; while either is null
  the row says so instead of inventing a number.
- ``plan_vs_actual.csv``: per host and month, the planned C_mon and repair pool against the
  actual operating cost and repair-side spend.
- ``wright.json`` beside them: the nightly learning-curve refit.

``write_export`` is what ``kintsugi econ cfo-export`` runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from kintsugi.econ import governor, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

SCENARIO_Q = (0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
EXPORT_DIR = Path("business") / "cfo_export"
PLACEHOLDER_STATUS = ("computed from disclosed PLACEHOLDER cash and fixed costs (A-73), "
                      "not the Architect's figures")  # fmt: skip


def _csv(header: Sequence[str], rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]]) -> str:
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(header)
    writer.writerows(rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def _money(x: float) -> str:
    return f"{x:.4f}"


def observed_coverage(actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> float:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    total = int(units["primary_n"]) + int(units["secondary_n"])
    return int(units["secondary_n"]) / total if total else 0.0


def economics_row(plan: BusinessPlan, host: str, c_p: float, c_s: float, q: float,
                  ) -> dict[str, float]:  # fmt: skip
    h = plan.host(host)
    e_cost = governor.expected_incident_cost(q, c_s, c_p)
    incidents = h.expected_remaining_incidents
    cogs = h.c_mon_usd_month + e_cost * incidents
    return {"e_cost": e_cost, "incident_month": e_cost * incidents, "cogs": cogs,
            "gm": governor.gross_margin(h.price_usd_month, cogs)}  # fmt: skip


def unit_economics(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        h = plan.host(host)
        row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
        meets = "yes" if row["gm"] >= plan.gm_floor else "no"
        rows.append([host, h.tier, _money(h.price_usd_month), _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                     _money(c_p), units["primary_n"], _money(c_s), units["secondary_n"],
                     phase or "all", f"{q:.3f}", _money(row["e_cost"]),
                     f"{h.expected_remaining_incidents:g}", _money(row["incident_month"]),
                     _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}",
                     f"{100 * plan.gm_floor:.1f}", meets])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "tier", "price_usd_month", "c_mon_usd_month", "c_primary_usd",
              "primary_n", "c_secondary_usd", "secondary_n", "cost_phase", "coverage_q",
              "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incidents_month", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct", "gm_floor_pct", "meets_floor")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def scenarios(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals, phase: str | None) -> str:
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    rows = []
    for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
        for q in SCENARIO_Q:
            row = economics_row(plan, host, c_p, c_s, q)
            rows.append([host, f"{q:.1f}", _money(row["e_cost"]), _money(row["incident_month"]),
                         _money(row["cogs"]), f"{100 * row['gm']:.1f}"])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("host", "coverage_q", "expected_incident_cost_usd", "incident_cost_month_usd",
              "cogs_month_usd", "gross_margin_pct")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def runway(plan_data: Mapping[str, Any], plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals,
           phase: str | None) -> str:  # fmt: skip
    company = plan_data.get("company") or {}
    cash, fixed = company.get("cash_usd"), company.get("fixed_costs_usd_month")
    header = ("cash_usd", "fixed_costs_usd_month", "revenue_usd_month", "cogs_usd_month",
              "net_burn_usd_month", "runway_months", "status")  # fmt: skip
    units = actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)
    c_p, c_s = float(units["primary_mean_usd"]), float(units["secondary_mean_usd"])
    q = observed_coverage(actuals, phase)
    revenue = sum(plan.host(h).price_usd_month for h in plan.hosts)
    cogs = sum(economics_row(plan, h, c_p, c_s, q)["cogs"] for h in plan.hosts)
    if cash is None or fixed is None:
        return _csv(header, [["", "", _money(revenue), _money(cogs), "", "",
                              "set company.cash_usd and company.fixed_costs_usd_month in "
                              "business/plan.json"]])  # fmt: skip
    burn = float(fixed) + cogs - revenue
    months = "infinite" if burn <= 0 else f"{float(cash) / burn:.1f}"
    status = PLACEHOLDER_STATUS if company.get("placeholder") else "computed"
    return _csv(header, [[_money(float(cash)), _money(float(fixed)), _money(revenue),
                          _money(cogs), _money(burn), months, status]])  # fmt: skip


def plan_vs_actual(plan: BusinessPlan, actuals: Actuals) -> str:
    months = sorted({s.month for s in actuals.spends})
    rows = []
    for month in months:
        for host in sorted(plan.hosts):
            h = plan.host(host)
            planned_pool = governor.pool(h.price_usd_month, plan.gm_floor, h.c_mon_usd_month)
            rehearsal = actuals.total(host=host, month=month, phase="rehearsal")
            spent = actuals.month_to_date(host, month)
            rows.append([month, host, _money(h.c_mon_usd_month),
                         _money(actuals.operating_cost(host, month)), _money(planned_pool),
                         _money(spent), _money(rehearsal)])  # fmt: skip
    header = ("month", "host", "planned_c_mon_usd", "actual_operating_usd",
              "planned_repair_pool_usd", "actual_repair_spend_usd",
              "rehearsal_spend_usd")  # fmt: skip
    return _csv(header, rows)


def learning_curve(actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every response's cost in the order it happened (date, then source run)."""
    lines = sorted(actuals.select(phase=None, kinds=("repair", "vaccination")),
                   key=lambda s: (s.date, s.source, s.ref))  # fmt: skip
    found = wright.refit([s.usd for s in lines])
    found["refs"] = [s.ref for s in lines]
    found["phases"] = sorted({s.phase for s in lines})
    return found


def export(plan_path: Path, actuals: Actuals) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The export's files and their contents (paths relative to ``business/cfo_export``)."""
    data = json.loads(Path(plan_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    live = bool(actuals.select(kinds=("repair", "vaccination")))
    phase = "live" if live else None  # until W runs, the rehearsals are the only observations
    meta = {"business_plan_sha": plan.sha, "cost_phase": phase or "all (rehearsal only)",
            "observed_coverage_q": round(observed_coverage(actuals, phase), 6),
            "unit_costs": actuals.unit_costs(phase=phase)}  # fmt: skip
    return {
        "unit_economics.csv": unit_economics(plan, actuals, phase),
        "scenarios.csv": scenarios(plan, actuals, phase),
        "runway.csv": runway(data, plan, actuals, phase),
        "plan_vs_actual.csv": plan_vs_actual(plan, actuals),
        "wright.json": json.dumps(learning_curve(actuals), indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        "meta.json": json.dumps(meta, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
    }


def write_export(repo: Path, actuals: Actuals, out: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
    folder = out or Path(repo) / EXPORT_DIR
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []
    for name, text in export(Path(repo) / "business" / "plan.json", actuals).items():
        (folder / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(folder / name)
    return written

"""The cfo.ai export and the nightly Wright refit (Stage 9)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from kintsugi.cli import main
from kintsugi.econ import cfo_sync, wright
from kintsugi.econ.actuals import Actuals, Spend
from kintsugi.econ.cortex import BusinessPlan

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PLAN = REPO / "business" / "plan.json"
EXPORT = REPO / "business" / "cfo_export"


def _rows(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)))


def test_the_committed_export_is_what_the_plan_and_actuals_give() -> None:
    files = cfo_sync.export(PLAN, Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json"))
    assert sorted(files) == sorted(p.name for p in EXPORT.iterdir())
    for name, text in files.items():
        assert (EXPORT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == text, name
    meta = json.loads(files["meta.json"])
    assert meta["business_plan_sha"] == BusinessPlan.load(PLAN).sha
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "all (rehearsal only)"  # no live spend before W
    triage = next(r for r in _rows(files["unit_economics.csv"]) if r["host"] == "triage")
    assert triage["meets_floor"] == "yes"
    assert float(triage["gross_margin_pct"]) >= 70.0
    assert len(_rows(files["scenarios.csv"])) == 3 * len(cfo_sync.SCENARIO_Q)
    assert "set company.cash_usd" in _rows(files["runway.csv"])[0]["status"]


def test_runway_is_computed_only_from_the_architects_numbers() -> None:
    data = json.loads(PLAN.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data["company"] = {"cash_usd": 10000.0, "fixed_costs_usd_month": 1000.0}
    plan = BusinessPlan.from_json(data)
    actuals = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json")
    row = _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]
    burn = 1000.0 + float(row["cogs_usd_month"]) - 697.0
    assert row["status"] == "computed"
    assert float(row["runway_months"]) == pytest.approx(10000.0 / burn, abs=0.05)
    data["company"]["fixed_costs_usd_month"] = 0.0
    assert _rows(cfo_sync.runway(data, plan, actuals, None))[0]["runway_months"] == "infinite"


def test_live_spend_replaces_the_rehearsal_unit_costs() -> None:
    live = Actuals.load(REPO / "business" / "actuals.json").add(
        Spend("2026-10-20", "triage", "repair", 2.0, "INC-0001", "case"),
        Spend("2026-10-21", "scout", "vaccination", 0.2, "VAC-AB-2-scout", "case"),
    )
    meta = json.loads(cfo_sync.export(PLAN, live)["meta.json"])
    assert meta["cost_phase"] == "live"
    assert meta["unit_costs"]["primary_mean_usd"] == 2.0
    assert meta["observed_coverage_q"] == 0.5


def test_the_refit_needs_three_points_and_recovers_the_exponent() -> None:
    assert wright.refit([1.0, 0.5])["status"] == "insufficient"
    costs = [wright.predict(n, 10.0, 0.4) for n in range(1, 9)]
    found = wright.refit(costs)
    assert found["status"] == "fitted"
    assert found["b"] == pytest.approx(0.4, abs=1e-6)
    assert found["progress_ratio"] == pytest.approx(2**-0.4, abs=1e-6)


def test_the_econ_commands(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path,
                           capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:  # fmt: skip
    monkeypatch.chdir(REPO)
    assert main(["econ", "refit"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["n_points"] == 4
    assert main(["econ", "cfo-export", "--out", str(tmp_path / "cfo")]) == 0
    assert (tmp_path / "cfo" / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        EXPORT / "unit_economics.csv").read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # fmt: skip
    capsys.readouterr()
    assert main(["econ", "actuals"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["rehearsal"]["secondary_n"] == 2

"""Post-commit checks (MASTER_HANDOFF §3): one Entire-Checkpoint trailer, its ref, files_touched
covers HEAD, no Co-authored-by, author identity, secret scan of the added lines."""

import subprocess
import sys

from kintsugi.memory import entire
from kintsugi.proof.redaction import scan_text


def git(*a: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                          check=True).stdout


msg = git("log", "-1", "--format=%B")
author = git("log", "-1", "--format=%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>").strip()
ids = [l.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for l in msg.splitlines() if l.startswith("Entire-Checkpoint:")]
ok = True
print("author/committer:", author)
if author != "Surya Prasanth R <suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com> | Surya Prasanth R <suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>":
    ok = False
    print("BAD author")
if "co-authored-by" in msg.lower():
    ok = False
    print("BAD co-author trailer")
if len(ids) != 1:
    ok = False
    print("BAD checkpoint trailers:", ids)
else:
    cid = ids[0]
    refs = [l for l in git("show-ref").splitlines() if cid in l]
    print("checkpoint", cid, "refs:", len(refs))
    ok &= len(refs) >= 1
    touched = set(entire.read_checkpoint(".", cid).metadata.get("files_touched") or [])
    diff = set(git("show", "--name-only", "--format=", "HEAD").split())
    missing = sorted(diff - touched)
    print("files:", len(diff), "missing from files_touched:", missing)
    ok &= not missing
added = "\n".join(l[1:] for l in git("show", "--format=", "-U0", "HEAD").splitlines()
                  if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++"))
findings = scan_text(added, where="HEAD")
print("secret findings:", len(findings))
ok &= not findings
print("OK" if ok else "FAILED")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

spec, sealed on arrival (Saboteur.seal) and queued (SabotageCampaign.request); the answer is the

SQLite, clients keyed by a salted hash. GET /api/state: ledger head, escalations, antibodies.

git add business/plan.json business/cfo_export/meta.json business/cfo_export/runway.csv kintsugi/econ/cfo_sync.py tests/econ/test_cfo_sync.py && ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
econ: disclosed placeholder cash and fixed costs so runway computes (A-73)

business/plan.json: company.cash_usd 250000.0 and fixed_costs_usd_month 18000.0, flagged
company.placeholder = true with a note saying they are illustrative seed-stage figures, not the
Architect's. kintsugi/econ/cfo_sync.py: while the flag is true, runway.csv's status says the
figures are disclosed placeholders (A-73) instead of "computed"; null figures still say what
to set. business/cfo_export/: regenerated with kintsugi econ cfo-export (runway 14.4 months at
a net burn of $17,376.27/month; meta.json pins the new plan sha 8e384b9f…). The evidence of
earlier rehearsals keeps the plan sha it ran against.
tests/econ/test_cfo_sync.py: the committed export carries the placeholder status and the
expected burn and runway; the plan labels its figures; null figures still say so.
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s'; uv run python -I "C:/Users/surya/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--myspace-hacckathons-kintsugi-omega-master/6ec8f922-2eb8-485f-8cc3-ee5110304556/scratchpad/verify_commit.py"
